translations.text: It shall come to pass that the sea will flow, a flood over the earth; life will be at an end for every single one. Often he who is willing may consider the truth in his own mind.
Our lord, highest of mighty kings, has appointed for himself to come here on the greatest day; then the ruler of mankind will burn up the land with fire. That is no small matter to speak of.

Heat will be kindled when fire seizes the corners of the earth, a burning flame seizing the bright creation; all this wide ground will be filled with embers, with fierce firebrands, just as fierce-minded men now hold sway,
who gain through boasting and strive to mock their Lord, until the guardians of sins deceive them, so that they seek hell with that troop and fly with the fiends.
For them there will be fire, a grievous torment, where day never shines with light from the sky. Instead it stays forever locked up, once the spirit is given over to terror.

Above, it is narrow, and within, it is hot; that is no excellent dwelling, but the greatest of terrors is there. Nor is it any joyful home; rather, the abyss of hell is there, a painful journey for the one who very often destroys peace with his mouth.
He does not know that dark creation, how it stands eternal, without end, for the one who is offered up there for his sins and then endures strife forever and ever.

Who then is so wise in spirit, or knows so much, that he could ever describe the height of the heavens, or describe as fully God's portion as it stands ready for pure hearts, for those who are willing to fear this saying, so deep as it is?
The day shall come when we bring forth each of our sins, our habits and our thoughts; that will be a severe assembly, a harsh host. Heat will be cooled.

Then there will be nothing in this world but the sound of water, the home of the fish; there will be no bone or blood here, but every child of men shall learn, in body and in soul, the reward for all that we did on earth before, whether good or evil.
No greater terror can come about in the world, and it will be widely known.
No star will shine here, but glory will have passed away, and the riches of the earth with it. Therefore I will always teach people to praise God's glory on high,
…may they live in faith with hopes of glory, and always work the love of the Lord in this world, before the proud day announces with trumpets the burning-hot flame, the overwhelming might of terror.
No man's glory will last any longer in this life once the Guardian of light sends fire over the whole expanse of the earth.

The power of the sky will flash, flame will rush on, bright and burning; bloodshed will be revealed to many, the punishment of the mighty King. All the bright creation will tremble, firebrands will leap on that deep day, and the heaven above will resound.
when men and women leave the world and the misery of earth; then they will look upon what they have earned for eternity.
Then it will be made known who has lived his life in purity; a reward will be ready for him.
There was always hope in heaven after our Saviour, the Ruler of middle-earth, was bound fast on the gleaming tree with the clasp of sorrow, through the greatest event of creation.
Christ knows all good deeds. The sinful soul has no reason to boast that heaven awaits it, when it very often despises holy teaching and turns it to mockery.
He knows nothing of that terror, has no understanding of the evil, until it falls upon him.

He will discover it then, when the sudden disaster comes and is made known to many throughout middle-earth, that he is worse off, set apart into the host on the left, than if he could go to the right hand, released from his sins.
Little does he think of that, the one who, glad with wine, enjoys his desires and sits merry at the feast. He does not mourn over his journey, or over how it may go for him after this world.
Then the Lord of spirits, the Prince of glory, will want to repay with favours, in keeping with that fate, the one who now thinks sorrowfully on his sins and endures great anxiety of mind;
the Ruler of life, the Shepherd of the heavens, will then reward him with good things after his journey from here, because he became so sad and sorrowful for his sins.
He who wishes to live with God, and to enjoy the dwelling that the bright Father, the lord of spirits, prepares for us, must not be too slow, nor too sluggish in these teachings.
It is the Lord of victory who adorns that hall and builds it splendidly. The pure, free of stains, shall [go] there, as the Ruler, King of all kings, said.
Therefore every living one among the deep-minded obeys the Lord, every one of those who wish to ascend to the height of the heavens.
Yet it will come to pass, though it be covered with dust, the body with clay, that it shall receive life, life after the earth.
The people will be summoned, all the children of Adam, to give account; then spirit and bone-house will be gathered, joined together for that journey.
Truth will make that known when we meet on the greatest day, men at the cross. Then they will tell many true things,
everything of hot and cold, of good or evil, that has happened under heaven; the highest of heavenly kings will listen closely to the deeds of men.

No one will ever sound a horn so loud or blow a trumpet so hard that the bright voice, the Ruler's word, will not be louder to people over all the earth. The plains will tremble at the message that he assigns to us all.
Answer this saying now. It shall be made known that I cannot turn aside what is fated under heaven, but it shall happen like this to every people over all the bright dwellings: burning fire.
Then, after the fire, life will be established; whoever thinks well now will have riches in glory.
